subject.title: Android node notification forwarding causes cross-session replies (WhatsApp duplicate sends to wrong group)

question: Should the fix primarily enforce outbound session/channel binding for node notification sessions, Android native-package suppression defaults, or gateway-side notification package filtering?
rationale: The source evidence shows the remaining behavior crosses Android notification policy, Gateway node events, and outbound channel sends; choosing the wrong owner could either miss the security boundary or add brittle package/config policy.

options.title: Harden outbound binding first
options.body: Reject or constrain cross-channel `message.send` from node notification sessions unless an explicit operator-approved route binding exists, then layer Android package filtering as defense in depth.

options.title: Suppress native packages in Android
options.body: Block known native-channel package IDs in Android notification forwarding defaults, which reduces duplicate inputs but depends on a maintained package list and may miss installed plugins.

options.title: Add Gateway package filtering
options.body: Add server-side notification package filtering for operators, which is useful defense in depth but adds config surface and does not by itself close unbound outbound sends.

recommendation.title: Harden outbound binding first
recommendation.body: Reject or constrain cross-channel `message.send` from node notification sessions unless an explicit operator-approved route binding exists, then layer Android package filtering as defense in depth.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision centers on the gateway/node-event behavior introduced in the Android notification event work, with Android policy contributors as adjacent reviewers.
